source.title: Spanning Training Progress: Temporal Dual-Depth Scoring (TDDS) for Enhanced Dataset Pruning
source.authors: Xin Zhang; Jia-Wei Du; Yun-Song Li; Wei-Ying Xie; Joey Tianyi Zhou

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies batch size during coreset training and reports test accuracy, bearing conceptually on V5. It does not measure training error or the train–test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The main pruning comparisons, architecture transfer results, and ablations do not measure the outcomes named in V1–V4, V6–V8. Table 6 and its accompanying text report the paper's own smaller-batch comparison, which bears on V5.
record.test_reason: Table 6 tests V5 in a new setting: ResNet-18 trained on aggressively pruned CIFAR coresets. Under the same 200-epoch budget, reducing batch size from 128 to 64 or 32 improves held-out accuracy. Training error is unnecessary for this batch-size comparison, but the proposed overfitting mechanism is not directly measured.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the batch-size discussion: smaller batches improve accuracy under aggressive pruning, and TDDS retains its advantage. The authors attribute this to reduced overfitting and greater optimization exploration, but do not directly measure that mechanism or a train–test gap. The paper's main conclusion is that TDDS improves dataset pruning by combining temporal contribution estimates with variability-based selection.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares batch sizes in dataset-pruning experiments using coreset training, rather than directly measuring the train–test gap in the original claim's settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes accuracy in the reported high-pruning coreset settings; the magnitude of change differs by dataset and pruning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: TDDS and other pruning methods select samples using temporal scores and report coreset accuracy, including architecture transfer and robustness experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Temporal sample-selection criteria can improve coreset performance. These comparisons do not test V8's influence-defined memorization criterion.

record.problems: The batch-size comparison is limited to CIFAR coreset training at pruning rates 80% and 90%; no training errors or direct train–test gaps are reported. The comparison changes batch size only within those pruned-data settings.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results meeting the row criteria for the listed versions were identified.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy. The 20% label-noise experiment does not establish these outcomes.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.

A batch-size threshold or broad batch-size sweep; language models; recovery of the larger-batch result through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes. Strategy-P varies duration without a crossed batch-size comparison, so it does not establish recovery of a batch-size penalty.
Controlled dropout or weight-decay removal comparisons.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking of train–test gaps.
Influence-defined memorization and removal of the most memorized examples versus equally sized random removals.

missing.what: Missing batch-size comparisons for seven other selection methods. CIFAR-10, 80% pruning, batch 128→64 accuracy: Random 86.92→88.87; Entropy 80.77→83.49; Forgetting 61.94→76.18; EL2N 59.28→68.64; AUM 59.11→69.60; Moderate 86.45→87.76; Dyn-Unc 73.28→79.76. Add separate rows with Table 6 uncertainties.

Missing CIFAR-10, 90% pruning, batch 128→32 comparisons: Random 76.71→83.77; Entropy 63.65→72.06; Forgetting 38.95→45.87; EL2N 23.54→31.89; AUM 30.62→34.74; Moderate 76.11→83.61; Dyn-Unc 31.99→37.12. Add separate rows with uncertainties.

Missing CIFAR-100, 80% pruning, batch 128→64 comparisons: Random 56.19→57.79; Entropy 38.55→42.86; Forgetting 38.11→38.42; EL2N 14.67→17.31; AUM 16.85→18.43; Moderate 54.22→56.52; Dyn-Unc 36.21→39.19. Add separate rows with uncertainties; the Forgetting difference is small relative to the reported variation.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V5. Table 6 places batch 64 only under 80% pruning and batch 32 only under 90% pruning. Its baseline methods are experiments performed in this study, not merely cited results.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and optimizer tuning.
Large batches beyond a workload-dependent threshold; language models; training-error comparisons; longer training, warmup, normalization, or regularization adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

tranche.reason: The paper compares batch sizes in aggressively pruned CIFAR coreset training, a new setting for the fixed-epoch batch-size claim.

source_check.notes: Inspected the extracted v3 text (abstract, introduction, Table 6 and surrounding setup, Appendix D, and conclusion); the rendered v3 PDF page 12 table image; and source_evidence.json. The paper attributes the small-batch effect to avoiding overfitting through optimization exploration, but does not directly measure that mechanism. First-check omission: it accepted the synthesis wording about highly imbalanced CIFAR without qualifying that this study tests aggressive pruning, not class imbalance.

statements.correction: For TDDS on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, Table 6 reports higher accuracy with smaller batches at 80% and 90% pruning under the 200-epoch setup. Appendix D says smaller batches improve accuracy at high pruning rates; the paper does not directly measure the proposed overfitting mechanism.
statements.problem: The TDDS comparisons at fixed pruning settings and 200 epochs are supported. The phrase “Highly imbalanced CIFAR” is not established by this paper’s evidence: it discusses aggressively pruned coresets and small available data, not a CIFAR class-imbalance experiment. The balanced-data curves and other cited studies are outside this study-specific check.
